content:
Nuevo Laredo's free two-day, drive-thru vaccination drive delivered 2,593 doses against influenza, COVID-19 and pneumococcus, the municipal government reported October 24 — 1,275 doses on day one and 1,318 on day two.

The drive was organized by the Secretaría de Bienestar Social and the Dirección de Salud Municipal, under Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, as fall-and-winter respiratory-season prevention. Residents could roll through without leaving their cars, a format the city has used to lower the barrier for families fitting health care around work and school.

The turnout matters beyond the headline number. Across the river, U.S. health officials reported the same week that seasonal flu activity is climbing earlier than usual — which makes a two-day, nearly 2,600-dose push in a border city a meaningful piece of binational prevention, not just a municipal statistic.

The city is not stopping at vaccines: its next “Empleo en tu Colonia” job fair lands Wednesday, October 28, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Plaza Hidalgo, with more than 200 vacancies from 15-plus employers across commercial, maquiladora, services and transport sectors, according to the municipal employment exchange.

What to watch next: whether the city repeats the drive-thru format as respiratory season deepens, and how the October 28 job fair turnout compares with the previous edition, which placed 50 people with Tri-Con de México.
